items.body:
# Axis vs Tori Finance: Two Pre-Token Yield Protocols, Two Different Bets

Both Axis and Tori Finance are DeFi yield protocols live before a native token. Their similarity stops there. One is building a market-neutral arbitrage engine with an early-access vault campaign. The other is packaging institutional FX carry into a retail stablecoin yield product with day-one DeFi integrations. This comparison looks at mechanism, growth path, and unresolved risks.

## Mechanism

Axis runs a delta-neutral arbitrage engine across crypto, USD, bitcoin, and gold exposures. Profits flow to USDx holders. The first live product is Origin Vault, accepting USDT or USDC with a stated 10-20% base APY and a 2x early multiplier. The protocol does not charge explicit user fees; returns come from spread capture.

Tori Finance issues trUSD, a synthetic dollar backed by delta-neutral FX carry positions. Users swap USDC or USDT for trUSD, then stake into strUSD to earn yield from money markets, futures arbitrage, and calendar spreads. Indicative APY is around 10.5%, with a reserve fund buffer behind trUSD. The docs show an unstake-then-exit flow, so liquidity depends on actual unstake terms rather than a simple "redeem anytime" claim.

## Growth

Axis is currently incentive-led. The Origin Vault campaign uses a $50M cap and 2x Coordinates multiplier to attract early depositors. Planned Ethereum availability and custody, oracle, and verification partnerships may broaden reach, but post-campaign retention is not yet supported by evidence.

Tori grew through pre-deposit onboarding and a referral-style entry link observed in its app URL. Day-one integrations with Pendle, Morpho, Royco, and Curve give it distribution inside existing DeFi. DefiLlama ranks Tori 14th among basis-trading protocols by TVL.

## Funding and team

Axis raised $5M in a seed round led by Galaxy Ventures in December 2025, with backers including FalconX and OKX Ventures. The team includes six named leaders with backgrounds at Alphanonce and QCP Capital, and LinkedIn profiles are verifiable.

Tori's seed round was led by Delphi Digital, though the amount is not independently confirmed. Only the founder, Samed Duzcay, is publicly identified, via a podcast interview. This makes Tori more opaque on team and capitalization.

## Risks

Axis' main unresolved question is net yield durability after the early multiplier ends. No audited protocol revenue or explicit fee schedule is public. The $50M vault cap creates a first-mover rush but also a cliff effect.

Tori's risk is strategy and smart-contract exposure. Yields are variable and can turn negative. The protocol is early with limited history. The actual exit path and slippage on unstake are not confirmed in the docs reviewed.

## Conclusion

Axis fits users who want market-neutral crypto and gold exposure through a single vault product and are comfortable with campaign-driven APY that may decline after the early multiplier ends.

Tori fits users who want delta-neutral FX carry exposure through a DeFi-native wrapper, can tolerate variable yield, and want access through existing platforms like Pendle or Morpho rather than a standalone vault experience.

Neither project has a native token, so both are still proving product-market fit. The meaningful difference is not "which pays more" but "which mechanism and distribution path you believe can sustain users after the campaign period."
